title: ⭐⭐ Revision: from the sentence to the whole text

questions.prompt: One form in this sentence is wrong: "Since the first satellite went up, we are using computers to explore space." Which correction does it need?

options.text: went up should become has gone up
are using should become have been using
are using should become were using
to explore should become for exploring

questions.explanation: "Since the first satellite went up" opens a period that starts in the past and reaches today, and such a period takes the present perfect; the activity has never stopped, so the form is the present perfect continuous: "are using should become have been using". "are using should become were using" only moves the mistake into another past and still cuts the link with today. "went up should become has gone up" spoils a form that is already right, because the launch is one finished event inside that past and a present perfect refuses a moment named that way. "to explore should become for exploring" replaces a correct infinitive of purpose: English uses something to do a thing.

questions.prompt: A hospital has bought machines that test how well the lungs work. Which phrase names them in correct English?

options.text: a lung-testing machine
a machine lung-testing
a machine of testing lungs
a testing lung machine

questions.explanation: English stacks the describing words in front of the noun they describe, so a machine that tests lungs is "a lung-testing machine". "a machine lung-testing" puts the describing words after the noun, which is the order of French, not of English. "a testing lung machine" keeps them in front but reverses them, and it now reads as a lung that is doing the testing. "a machine of testing lungs" builds a heavy of-phrase where English uses the compound.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The new bypass has cut the journey to the coast by twenty minutes. ___, the number of accidents on the old road has not fallen."

options.text: Besides
In fact
However
Therefore

questions.explanation: The second sentence sets a disappointing fact against the good news of the first, and the linker that opens a contrast at the head of a sentence is "However". "Therefore" would present the unchanged number of accidents as the result of the faster journey, which reverses the sense completely. "Besides" adds one more argument pushing in the same direction as the first sentence. "In fact" confirms or sharpens what has just been said; it never contradicts it.

questions.prompt: In a business letter, which line comes immediately before the first paragraph of the body?

options.text: 9 Rue de Marseille, Tunis
Dear Mrs Trabelsi,
Executive director
Yours faithfully,

questions.explanation: The salutation is the last line before the body begins, so the letter reads "Dear Mrs Trabelsi," and then starts its first paragraph. "9 Rue de Marseille, Tunis" is an address, and both addresses belong to the head of the page, above the salutation, beside the date. "Yours faithfully," is the closing formula and sits under the last line of the body. "Executive director" is a job title and belongs to the signature block, the very last one on the page.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a habit that belonged to the past and has stopped?

options.text: My grandfather has walked to the mill every morning.
My grandfather is used to walking to the mill every morning.
My grandfather walked to the mill yesterday morning.
My grandfather used to walk to the mill every morning.

questions.explanation: Used to followed by the base verb is the structure kept for a habit that is over, so the sentence is "My grandfather used to walk to the mill every morning." "My grandfather is used to walking to the mill every morning." uses be used to, which says he is accustomed to the walk and still takes it, a present state. "My grandfather has walked to the mill every morning." ties the habit to today with a present perfect, so it has not stopped either. "My grandfather walked to the mill yesterday morning." reports one single walk on one named morning, not a habit at all.

questions.prompt: Arrange these five sentences so that they form one coherent paragraph.

options.text: In 1902 a young clerk in Bizerte was told that his handwriting was too slow for the office.
He spent every evening of that winter copying a page of the newspaper.
Within two years he was writing faster than anybody else on his floor.
His employers then asked him to train the new clerks.
Today the school he opened still carries his name.

questions.explanation: The time markers give the order away, and each sentence leans on the one in front of it. The sentence dated 1902 is the only one that can open: it names the clerk and states his problem, and everything after it says He or his. The evenings of that winter are his answer to that problem, so they come second. Within two years measures a result from that winter of work, so it comes third. Then points back at that result and can never open a paragraph. Today closes the distance between 1902 and the present, so it comes last. The classic mistake is to start with Today, which sounds like an opening line but leaves then and Within two years with nothing to lean on.
